findings.text: NCI links NCT05208047 to CGT9486-21-301. The study has multiple parts; the imatinib-only pretreatment population in Part 2 matches this GIST application. Whole-study planned enrollment cannot replace the randomized analysis count.

Sponsor reports PFS HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.39-0.65), p<0.0001, with medians 16.5 versus 9.2 months against active sunitinib. The magnitude and precision support efficacy; independent protocol/SAP and censoring review remain necessary.

SEC presentation reports ORR 45.6% versus 25.8%, a 19.8-point difference; issuer releases round these to 46% versus 26%. This supports activity, while multiplicity and hierarchy require the original SAP.

SEC slides report 413 randomized: 204 combination, 209 control. Randomization and blinded central PFS assessment support interpretability. Open treatment assignment still permits bias requiring review; this is not proof of an unbiased dataset.

Reported grade 3+ ALT/AST elevations were 10.8% versus 1.4%. The imbalance is an opposing benefit-risk consideration, not proof of rejection; exposure, reversibility and clinical consequences require independent evaluation.

Treatment-related discontinuation was reported as 7.4% versus 3.8%. Safety denominators in the SEC presentation are 204 and 208 dosed patients, whereas randomized counts are 204 and 209. Do not interchange those denominators.
Issuer describes OS as immature. This prevents a firm survival conclusion, but immature OS alone is not a demonstrated FDA failure criterion for GIST.

The May 28 issuer disclosure reports NDA acceptance, Priority Review and a November 30, 2026 target for the GIST combination. Filing acceptance establishes neither approval nor absence of later review issues.

FDA authors discuss robust, clinically meaningful PFS with acceptable benefit-risk as a GIST approval basis. Selected approvals contextualize the endpoint; they do not estimate approval odds for PEAK or validate transfer across treatment lines.
